title: Euclid: Infinitely Many Primes
status: **Proved** (classical; Euclid, Elements IX.20). Status closed; pedagogy of the *idea* remains active.
theorem_line: There are infinitely many primes. Proof idea: from finite list $p_1,\ldots,p_k$, form $N=P+1$ with $P=\prod p_i$; any prime factor of $N$ is new.
videos: blackpenredpen — Euclid's proof infinitely many primes
Wrath of Math — Proof: infinitely many primes
Maths and Stats — Number Theory: Infinitude of Primes (Euclid)
papers: Proofs that there are infinitely many primes (math encyclopedia style)
web: Stanford Encyclopedia-style / intro number theory notes (search Euclid primes)
definitions: Integer $p>1$ whose only positive divisors are $1$ and $p$.
Given primes $p_1,\ldots,p_k$, set $N=p_1\cdots p_k+1$. $N$ need not be prime.
confusions: Claiming $N$ itself is always prime (false; e.g. $2\cdot3\cdot5\cdot7\cdot11\cdot13+1=30031=59\cdot509$).
Confusing infinitude with a formula for the $n$th prime.

title: Cantor's Diagonal Argument
status: **Proved** (Cantor). Uncountability of $\mathbb{R}$ / power set of $\mathbb{N}$ is standard theorem; representation hygiene is the main student pitfall.
theorem_line: No surjection $\mathbb{N}\to\{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}}$ (equivalently $\mathbb{R}$ is uncountable). Diagonal flips $a_{nn}$ to build an escaped sequence.
videos: Numberphile — Infinity is bigger than you think (James Grime / Cantor)
papers: Stillwell / standard set-theory texts (Roads to Infinity style)
definitions: In bijection with a subset of $\mathbb{N}$ (or finite).
Given listed sequences $a_i=(a_{i1},a_{i2},\ldots)$, define $b_n \\neq a_{nn}$ so $b$ is not any $a_i$.
confusions: Applying diagonalization naively to $\mathbb{Q}$ (rationals *are* countable).
Ignoring dual expansions $0.1999\ldots=0.2000\ldots$ without a digit rule that avoids both.

title: Gödel's Incompleteness Theorems
status: **Proved** (Gödel 1931). First and second incompleteness theorems are theorems of mathematical logic; popularizations often overclaim 'math is broken'.
theorem_line: Any consistent, effectively axiomatized theory capable of arithmetic is incomplete: there are true (in $\mathbb{N}$) sentences unprovable in the theory. Second: such a theory cannot prove its own consistency (under standard formalizations).
videos: Numberphile — Gödel's Incompleteness Theorem (Marcus du Sautoy)
TED-Ed — Paradox at the heart of mathematics (du Sautoy)
Veritasium — Math's Fundamental Flaw (Gödel + undecidability arc)
papers: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy — Gödel's incompleteness
N. Raatikainen SEP entry (same as above)
definitions: Language + effective axioms + rules of inference; theorems = derivable sentences.
Self-referential arithmetical sentence asserting its own unprovability in $T$.
confusions: Interpreting incompleteness as 'nothing can be proved' or 'all systems are inconsistent'.
Conflating incompleteness with undecidability of arbitrary natural-language questions.

title: Euler and the Königsberg Bridges
status: **Proved** (Euler 1736 necessity; full sufficiency of Eulerian criteria completed later, Hierholzer). Founding theorem of graph theory.
theorem_line: A connected graph has an Eulerian circuit iff every vertex has even degree; an Eulerian trail iff exactly 0 or 2 odd-degree vertices. Königsberg multigraph has four odd vertices → impossible.
videos: Numberphile — Seven Bridges of Königsberg (Cliff Stoll)
TED-Ed — How the Königsberg bridge problem changed mathematics
Sarada Herke — Graph Theory: Seven Bridges of Konigsberg
Dr. Trefor Bazett — Euler Paths & 7 Bridges
definitions: Number of edge ends at a vertex (loops contribute 2).
Closed / open walk using each edge exactly once.
confusions: Thinking the answer depends on bridge lengths or geometry (only incidence matters).
Mixing Hamiltonian (vertices once) with Eulerian (edges once).

title: Irrationality of √2
status: **Proved** (classical Pythagorean / Euclidean tradition). Many independent proofs (parity, descent, unique factorization, geometric Apostol).
theorem_line: $\sqrt{2}$ is irrational: if $a/b$ in lowest terms with $a^2=2b^2$, then $a$ and $b$ are both even — contradiction.
videos: D!NG — A Proof That The Square Root of Two Is Irrational
Wrath of Math — Most Beautiful Proof √2 irrational (Apostol geometric)
Tipping Point Math — 5 Best Proofs √2 irrational
papers: Wikipedia — Square root of 2 / proofs of irrationality
definitions: From a positive integer solution produce a strictly smaller one — impossible.
confusions: Thinking the proof only works for √2 and not primes $p\equiv 3\pmod 4$ etc. without adapting the parity argument.
Confusing irrationality with transcendence.

title: Four Color Theorem (Computer-Assisted Proof)
status: **Proved** (Appel–Haken 1976; simplified/verified later, Robertson et al., computer-checked formalizations). Philosophical debate about computer proofs is separate from theorem status.
theorem_line: Every planar graph is 4-colorable (equivalently, every map on the plane/sphere can be colored with 4 colors so adjacent regions differ). Proof architecture: unavoidable set of reducible configurations + discharging.
videos: Numberphile — Four Color Map Theorem (James Grime)
Quanta — Math's Map Coloring Problem / first computer-assisted proof
Up and Atom — Four Color Theorem: What Counts as a Proof?
papers: Robertson, Sanders, Seymour, Thomas — new proof survey (1997 era)
web: Quanta Magazine related articles (map coloring / computer proofs)
definitions: Graph drawable in the plane without edge crossings.
Local pattern that cannot appear in a minimal counterexample.
confusions: Thinking 4 colors are needed for *every* map (many need fewer; 4 is worst-case bound).
Conflating 'computer-assisted' with 'unverified' after modern checks.

title: Fermat's Last Theorem (Wiles)
status: **Proved** (Wiles 1995, with Taylor; modularity for semistable elliptic curves + Ribet). Status closed; full modularity theorem later completed by others.
theorem_line: No positive integers $a,b,c,n$ with $n>2$ satisfy $a^n+b^n=c^n$. Modern idea: Frey curve from a hypothetical solution would be a non-modular semistable elliptic curve, contradicting Wiles–Taylor modularity + Ribet.
videos: Numberphile — Bridges to Fermat's Last Theorem (Ken Ribet)
Numberphile Podcast — FLT with Ken Ribet
papers: Wikipedia — Wiles's proof of Fermat's Last Theorem
Cambridge Maths feature — 30 years since announcement
Wiles, Modular elliptic curves and Fermat's Last Theorem, Annals 1995 (paywall/library)
web: Clay / public expositions of modularity idea
definitions: Smooth cubic curve $y^2=x^3+Ax+B$ with group law.
From $a^n+b^n=c^n$ form $y^2=x(x-a^n)(x+b^n)$ — too exotic to be modular if non-modular cases existed.
confusions: Claiming Wiles proved full modularity for all elliptic curves in 1995 (he proved the semistable case needed for FLT).
Treating popular documentaries as proofs.

title: Poincaré Conjecture (Perelman)
status: **Proved** (Perelman 2002–2003, Ricci flow with surgery completing Hamilton's program). Only solved Clay Millennium Problem as of 2026.
theorem_line: Every simply connected closed 3-manifold is homeomorphic to $S^3$. Stronger: Thurston geometrization (Perelman). Method: Ricci flow $\\partial_t g=-2\\operatorname{Ric}$ with surgery at singularities + entropy/monotonicity controls.
videos: Aleph 0 — Poincaré Conjecture and Ricci Flow
papers: Perelman arXiv papers (entropy formula / Ricci flow with surgery)
definitions: Every loop can be continuously contracted to a point.
Metric evolves by $\\partial_t g_{ij}=-2R_{ij}$, smoothing geometry like heat flow.
confusions: Thinking Perelman only proved Poincaré and not geometrization (he sketched geometrization).
Confusing topological $S^3$ characterization with smooth exotic structures in higher dimensions.

title: Mathematics of AI / Deep Learning
status: **Active research field.** Core engineering practice is mature; mathematical understanding of deep learning (generalization, optimization landscapes, feature learning) remains partial as of 2026.
theorem_line: Universal approximation (classical) is a *representation* theorem, not a training theorem. Training is empirical risk minimization via SGD on nonconvex $L(\\theta)$. Generalization of overparameterized nets is not settled by classical VC alone.
videos: 3Blue1Brown — But what is a neural network?
3Blue1Brown — Gradient descent, how neural networks learn
papers: Goodfellow, Bengio, Courville — Deep Learning (book site)
Double descent literature hub (Belkin et al. 2019)
confusions: Universal approximation ⇒ training finds the approximator.
Equating product demos with mathematical theorems.

title: Quantum Information
status: **Mature mathematical framework** (states, channels, entanglement) with **engineering frontiers** (fault tolerance, NISQ algorithms). Shor/Grover are theorems in the circuit model; physical scalability is experimental.
theorem_line: Qubit state $|\psi\\rangle=\\alpha|0\\rangle+\\beta|1\\rangle$ in $\\mathbb{C}^2$; multipartite systems use tensor products. Unitary evolution + measurement projectors. No-cloning is a theorem; Bell nonlocality is experimentally confirmed.
videos: Michael Nielsen — Quantum computing for the determined (playlist)
Veritasium — How does a quantum computer work?
Veritasium — How to make a quantum bit
Ronald de Wolf — Intro to Quantum Computing (lecture 1)
papers: Nielsen & Chuang — Quantum Computation and Quantum Information
definitions: Unit vector in $\\mathbb{C}^2$ up to global phase; density matrices for mixed states.
Non-product multipartite state; cannot write as $|\\psi\\rangle\\otimes|\\phi\\rangle$.
confusions: Thinking measurement 'computes all answers at once' without readout/post-processing structure.
Conflating QKD with post-quantum classical crypto.

title: Mathematical Biology
status: **Broad applied field.** ODE/PDE population models are classical; stochastic chemical kinetics, spatial pattern formation, and data-driven inference remain active.
theorem_line: SIR-type compartment models: $\\dot S=-\\beta SI$, $\\dot I=\\beta SI-\\gamma I$, $\\dot R=\\gamma I$. Threshold $R_0=\\beta/\\gamma$ governs invasion. Pattern formation via Turing instability is a classical PDE mechanism.
videos: 3Blue1Brown — Epidemic modeling / differential equations (related DE series)
Numberphile / popular SIR explainers (search SIR model)
definitions: Expected secondary cases from one infectious in a fully susceptible population.
Infection term $\\beta SI$ in well-mixed ODEs.
confusions: Treating ODE forecasts as exact predictions without parameter/structural uncertainty.
Ignoring stochastic extinction in small populations.

title: Network Science
status: **Active interdisciplinary field.** Erdős–Rényi, small-world, scale-free models are classical baselines; inference and dynamics on networks remain research-active.
theorem_line: ER random graphs $G(n,p)$ have giant component threshold $p\\sim 1/n$. Preferential attachment (Barabási–Albert) yields power-law degree tails under stated mechanisms — empirical claims need careful statistics.
videos: Barabási — Network Science: From Abstract to Physical (UiO)
Barabási — DTU Ørsted Lecture: Architecture of Complexity
Systems Innovation — Centralized & Scale Free Networks
confusions: Assuming all real networks are scale-free without statistical tests.
Confusing correlation with causal influence on graphs.

title: Future Cryptography (PQC & Beyond)
status: **Standards evolving.** NIST released first PQC FIPS (203–205) in 2024; migration is ongoing. QKD is a different technology stack from classical PQC algorithms.
theorem_line: Shor's algorithm breaks RSA/ECC on a large fault-tolerant quantum computer (theorem in circuit model). PQC bases security on lattice/code/hash/isogeny-type problems believed hard for quantum adversaries — hardness is *conjectural*, not proved.
videos: IBM Research — NIST post-quantum standards webcast
definitions: Classical crypto designed to resist quantum adversaries.
Ability to swap algorithms as standards/attacks evolve.
confusions: Assuming quantum computers already break RSA at scale today.
Equating QKD with PQC (different trust and deployment models).

title: Complexity Theory
status: **P vs NP remains open** (as of 2026). NP-completeness theory is mature; circuit lower bounds and derandomization are major frontiers.
theorem_line: Cook–Levin: SAT is NP-complete. Thousands of natural problems are NP-complete via poly-time reductions. P=NP? is open; most experts conjecture P≠NP.
videos: Michael Sipser — Beyond Computation: P vs NP (Harvard)
Quanta — Biggest Puzzle in CS: P vs NP (course-linked)
definitions: P: decidable in poly time. NP: verifiable in poly time given a witness.
Poly-time many-one map preserving yes/no answers.
confusions: Thinking NP means 'not polynomial' (it means nondeterministic poly / verifiable).
Claiming AI solves NP-complete problems 'in general' in poly time.

title: High-Dimensional Geometry
status: **Classical + modern probability.** Concentration of measure and JL lemma are theorems; geometric aspects of data analysis remain active.
theorem_line: Concentration: Lipschitz functions on high-dimensional spheres/Gaussians are nearly constant. Johnson–Lindenstrauss: $n$ points in Euclidean space embed in $O(\\varepsilon^{-2}\\log n)$ dimensions preserving distances up to $1\\pm\\varepsilon$.
videos: Simons Institute — High Dimensional Geometry and Concentration I
papers: Vershynin — High-Dimensional Probability (book PDF via author)
definitions: A r.v. $X$ concentrates if $P(|X-\\mathbb{E}X|>t)$ decays rapidly in $t$.
Effective degrees of freedom of a data set, often $\\ll$ ambient $d$.
confusions: Thinking all high-d phenomena are 'curses' (concentration also enables algorithms).
Ignoring that data often lie near low-dimensional structures.

title: Optimal Transport
status: **Mature theory, booming applications.** Monge–Kantorovich theory classical; Sinkhorn/entropic OT and gradient flows are modern computational engines.
theorem_line: Kantorovich problem: $\\inf_{\\pi\\in\\Pi(\\mu,\\nu)}\\int c\\,d\\pi$. Wasserstein-$p$ metrizes weak convergence (on suitable spaces). Brenier: under conditions, optimal maps are gradients of convex potentials.
videos: Simons — Crash Course on Optimal Transport
definitions: Entropic regularization of OT solved by matrix scaling.
confusions: Thinking OT always yields a deterministic Monge map in discrete equal-mass unbalanced settings without hypotheses.
Ignoring sample complexity blow-up of empirical W_p in high dimension.

title: Machine Learning Theory
status: **Active.** Classical PAC/VC is theorem-complete for uniform convergence regimes; modern deep learning theory (interpolation, implicit bias, double descent) is incomplete.
theorem_line: PAC learnability linked to finite VC dimension for binary classification (fundamental theorem of statistical learning, rough statement). Uniform convergence controls generalization for restricted classes; interpolating deep nets need other stories.
videos: Sipser / complexity contrast videos (hardness vs learnability culture)
papers: Belkin et al. — Reconciling modern ML and bias-variance (double descent)
definitions: Learn hypothesis with error $\\le\\varepsilon$ with probability $\\ge 1-\\delta$ from poly samples.
Size of largest shattered set; measures binary classifier class complexity.
confusions: Applying classical U-shaped bias-variance as universal law after the interpolation peak.
Reading empirical scaling laws as theorems.

title: Mathematical Physics
status: **Broad interface.** Many physical PDEs have incomplete global theories; Navier–Stokes regularity is a Clay Millennium Problem (**open** as of 2026). QFT axiomatization partial.
theorem_line: Navier–Stokes (Clay): global existence and smoothness of smooth finite-energy solutions to 3D incompressible NS on $\\mathbb{R}^3$ is open. Spectral theorem / operator theory underpin QM rigorously in standard settings.
videos: Clay — Luis Caffarelli, Navier–Stokes existence and smoothness
Clay — Vladimir Šverak, report on Navier–Stokes
web: Wikipedia — Yang–Mills existence and mass gap
definitions: Rigorous analysis of structures motivated by physics (not the same as theoretical physics practice).
Solution in a distributional / energy space sense, possibly singular.
confusions: Thinking physicists' successful numerical NS simulations close the Clay problem.
Conflating effective field theory practice with complete constructive QFT.
